title: Saul, Israel's First King
lead: Israel's first king, a tall Benjaminite from Gibeah, about 1030–1010 BC. Anointed by Samuel and acclaimed after a victory, he was later rejected by God, hunted David, and died in battle on Mount Gilboa.

sections.b: Saul is introduced looking for his father's lost donkeys and finds a kingdom (1 Samuel 9–10). Samuel anoints him in secret, the lot picks him out in public at Mizpah, and he proves himself by rescuing Jabesh-gilead from the Ammonites (1 Samuel 10–11). His reign then goes wrong: he offers a sacrifice without waiting for Samuel (1 Samuel 13), spares the Amalekite king (1 Samuel 15), and turns his jealousy on David (1 Samuel 18–26). On the night before his last battle he consults a medium at Endor (1 Samuel 28), and he and his sons die on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31). David mourns him in the Song of the Bow (2 Samuel 1:19–27). Hosea's "days of Gibeah" (Hosea 9:9; Hosea 10:9) may recall the crime of Judges 19 or, as some think, Saul's kingship, and Paul, a Benjaminite named Saul, recalls his namesake (Acts 13:21).
